about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

the switch has only an empty default arm, so the value switched on matters only if it is null (a NullPointerException); the mutant switches on task.aid() when it is non-null, and task.aid() is never null (EquivalenceRunTest gives a task the scenario's AID, a LINKed task takes its caller's: CicsTask `this.aid = caller.aid`)

task.linkArea() is non-null only when a det-port program LINKs ABNDPROC with its COMMAREA's bytes (CicsTask.link); the case starts ABNDPROC directly with a DTO COMMAREA, so the raw-area copy never runs. Killed by a case where a CBSA caller's det port LINKs ABNDPROC (its abend path)

the restore of the TRUNC mode in runTask's finally matters only to code that runs after the task in the same JVM under another mode; ABNDPROC's callers are CBSA programs, each translated with the same TRUNC(STD) (the cases' compiler options) and setting it on entry, so the mode left behind is the one they run under
